https://devjohn.site/about/
About John Mwaura
I am John Mwaura, known online as Dev John, an independent web and software developer in Kenya. I have worked since 2023, building business websites, online stores, custom software and automation. I also founded ABC Systems. I work across the full product: what a visitor sees, the database behind it, the APIs that connect it to other tools and the deployment. That can mean a small website with a clear enquiry route, or a business application with accounts, reports and payment workflows. My work starts with the task someone needs to complete. A shop customer wants to find an item and place an order. A member of staff needs the right information to do their job. A citizen looking through public spending needs records that are understandable and searchable. Those needs shape the interface and the code. Quick facts Name John Mwaura Also known as Dev John or Dev.John Location Kenya Working since 2023 Main work Websites, online stores, custom software and automation Languages and tools TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Next.js, Node.js and PostgreSQL Time zone East Africa Time, UTC+3, without daylight saving Reply time Within 24 hours Contact mwaura.ke.john@gmail.com What I build For a business website, I focus on clear service information, useful pages and an easy next action. A visitor on a phone should be able to understand what you offer and contact you without searching through a crowded layout. See my business website development service . An online store has a different job. Products need categories and useful details, and the cart, checkout and order handling need to fit the business. I work with M-Pesa and Stripe where they suit the agreed scope. My e-commerce development page explains the starter store. Custom software brings forms, business rules, reporting and an admin interface together around a specific workflow. I build dashboards and internal tools as well as public applications. Read about custom software development and the difference between a small scoped project and a larger platform. Automation connects actions that would otherwise need repeated manual work. That can include capturing an enquiry from WhatsApp, sending an order notification or syncing information with an existing tool. The WhatsApp automation service covers those possibilities. How I work These are the four principles on my homepage. They apply whether the project is a landing page or a platform with a database and integrations. I choose the technology after understanding the business problem and keep the whole path to launch in view. Business Problems Before Technology I start with the problem and the people, then pick the tools. End-to-End Ownership Database, APIs, deployment and maintenance, all handled. Built for Real-World Usage Mobile-first, payment-ready and practical. Performance, Security & Reliability Maintainable code that stays fast, safe and stable. Languages and tools I use React, Next.js and TypeScript for interfaces, and Node.js, PostgreSQL, Supabase and Prisma for backend work. Docker and GitHub Actions are part of the deployment tools on my homepage. M-Pesa Daraja and the WhatsApp Cloud API connect applications to payments and customer conversations. A single focused page has a different scope from a site with separate pages for several services. More custom design also means more decisions about the structure, content and presentation. Integrations such as M-Pesa or Stripe bring payment flows into the project. The required connection, the provider access and the behaviour after a payment all need to be described. An admin area can range from a small set of forms to several staff roles and detailed reports. For a shop, the number of products and the information attached to each product affect the work. Product variations, stock handling and order workflows should be discussed before treating them as included. The starter package lists a catalogue, categories, cart, checkout, order management and basic store administration. Content needs are part of the conversation too. Tell me whether the wording, product details and photos are ready, or whether writing and photography still need to be arranged. Let me know your intended deadline so we can discuss it with the rest of the scope. No delivery time is promised by these package prices. How a project runs Message me with the business goal and the kind of website or software you need. We discuss the requirements and agree what the project covers. You get a written quote for the agreed scope. I build the website or application around those requirements. You review the work and we discuss it against the scope. The project moves to launch. A useful first message explains who will use the result and what they should be able to do. If you already have a site, include its address and explain the part that needs attention. This gives the discussion more substance than choosing a package from the price alone. KSh and USD figures I show both currencies together so local and overseas clients can compare the published starting points. The exact figure is confirmed in writing when the scope is agreed. The two displayed figures are package starting prices, not a live exchange-rate calculator. For clients outside Kenya, the international project guide explains remote communication and time zone overlap. The project enquiry form includes budget and timeline fields, so you can send the context with your message. Pricing questions What is the lowest starting price? The Landing Page package starts at KSh 10,000 or $100. It covers one responsive page, WhatsApp and click-to-call buttons, a contact or enquiry form, basic on-page SEO and clear calls to action. How much does a small business website cost? Basic Website starts at KSh 15,000 or $150 for up to 3 pages. Business Website starts at KSh 20,000 or $200 for up to 5 pages. The final choice depends on the information and functionality you need. What does an online store start at? E-commerce Website starts at KSh 35,000 or $350. The exact payment integration and store requirements are agreed per project. Is custom software always KSh 40,000 or $400? No. That is a starting price for smaller, clearly scoped projects. Marketplaces, SaaS, booking platforms, complex API work and other advanced products need a custom quote. Is a product catalogue the same as a shop? A catalogue showcase presents products or services. A shop also needs a cart, checkout and order handling. The Professional Website package lists a showcase; the E-commerce Website package lists those shop features. Can M-Pesa or Stripe change the scope? Yes. Payment integration needs to match the checkout and business workflow. Tell me which payment flow you need so the connection can be included in the agreed quote. Can I discuss the budget before choosing a package? Yes. Send the business goal, required features and your budget through WhatsApp, email or the project form. I reply within 24 hours. Are these final fixed prices? No. Every figure is a starting price. The final price depends on the functionality and scope agreed, and the exact amount is confirmed in writing. https://devjohn.site/services/
Web and software development services
I build websites, online stores, APIs, dashboards and automation as an independent web and software developer in Kenya. My name is John Mwaura, and I work as Dev John. The starting package and final quote depend on what the project needs to do. Full-stack product development I build the interface, database and backend as parts of one product. Authentication, data structure and deployment belong in the same discussion as the screens people use. A small internal application and a public platform can both need full-stack work, with very different scopes. The custom software guide explains how I separate a clearly bounded project from a larger product. Read about full-stack product development API architecture and systems integration When two systems need to exchange information, an API defines how that exchange happens. I work on backend services, payment connections, webhooks and authentication flows. The starting point is the data that needs to move and the action that should follow. Provider access and the existing system need review before an integration can become part of the agreed scope. E-commerce and payment platforms An online store needs product information, a cart, checkout and a way for the business to handle orders. I build those parts together and work with M-Pesa Daraja and Stripe where appropriate. The starter package includes basic store administration. More detailed inventory rules, customer workflows or reporting need to be discussed against the actual store requirements. Read about e-commerce and payment platforms WhatsApp automation and customer workflows A customer message can start a lead record, an order workflow or a notification to a business tool. I use the WhatsApp Cloud API to connect conversations with these actions. The useful question is what happens after the message arrives. Automation should have a defined task, the information it needs and a clear place for that information to go. Read about whatsapp automation and customer workflows Dashboards and internal operations systems I build reporting interfaces and administrative tools for people running a business or platform. These can include role-based access, audit trails and operational records. Before choosing charts or screens, we need to know which decisions staff make and which records they need. The amount of custom reporting and access control affects whether the work fits a small project or an advanced platform. Performance engineering and technical SEO A page needs to load, respond to input and make its content understandable to search engines. My work includes Core Web Vitals checks, caching, structured data and technical SEO. Clear headings and readable page content matter alongside the code. Technical improvements remove obstacles to discovery, but they do not create a guarantee of search positions or business results. Cloud deployment and DevOps Getting software into production involves environments, deployment pipelines and the infrastructure around the application. My stack includes Docker, GitHub Actions, Linux and Nginx. The appropriate setup depends on the product and its requirements. Tell me about the existing hosting environment if there is one, so deployment work can be discussed with the rest of the project rather than assumed from a page price. Public sector and civic-tech platforms I build public-data and accountability interfaces, with UWAZI as my flagship example in Kenya. Civic technology can involve searchable records, case management and information presented for public use. The data model and the interface both matter. A project discussion needs to cover who supplies the records, how people will use them and which parts of the workflow need software. Which one do I need? Start with the action you want someone to take. If visitors need to learn about your business and send an enquiry, a business website may be enough. Selling products through a cart and checkout points towards an online store. A product showcase without checkout can fit a website package instead. If staff are copying records between spreadsheets, or you need forms and reports tied to business rules, describe that workflow as a custom software enquiry. If most of the work starts in customer messages, explain the WhatsApp conversation and what should happen next. You do not need to choose the technology before contacting me. Compare the published starting prices , browse my projects and send the requirements . I reply within 24 hours. https://devjohn.site/services/web-development/
Business website development
I build business websites for shops, clinics, restaurants, tradespeople, schools and small companies. I am John Mwaura, known as Dev John, a web and software developer in Kenya. A landing page starts at KSh 10,000 or $100, with the final price based on the agreed scope. Give visitors the information they came for A business website should explain what you do, who the service is for and how to get in touch. A clinic may need separate service information and a clear contact route. A restaurant needs a useful presentation of its food and business details. A tradesperson needs to show the work and make an enquiry easy. I start with those visitor tasks rather than a long list of effects. Clear headings, readable text and a practical mobile layout help someone understand the business. A WhatsApp button or enquiry form gives them a next step, with the exact contact features determined by the package. Website packages and their boundaries Landing Page starts at KSh 10,000 or $100 for one responsive page. It includes WhatsApp and click-to-call buttons, a contact or enquiry form, basic on-page SEO and clear calls to action. It suits a focused service, product or campaign that does not need several separate pages. Basic Website starts at KSh 15,000 or $150 for up to 3 pages. The package covers a responsive layout, business and service information, contact details, WhatsApp, a contact form and basic SEO. Business Website starts at KSh 20,000 or $200 for up to 5 pages, adding customised business-focused design, about, services and contact sections, with social and location links where appropriate. Professional Website starts at KSh 30,000 or $300 for up to 8 pages. It allows more detailed layouts, expanded information and a product or service catalogue showcase. A showcase is different from a store with a cart and checkout. For online ordering through a shop, read about e-commerce website development . Mobile speed and local search People may open a business site on a phone using a limited data connection. I consider image size, page structure and how much the browser needs to load. Contact controls should be easy to reach, and a visitor should not have to zoom into tiny text to understand a service. Basic on-page SEO includes making page topics understandable through titles, descriptions, headings and content. Relevant business and location information should be accurate. Technical SEO can support search discovery, but no website package guarantees a Google position. Existing sites may also need a separate performance or technical review. Custom software development
I build custom software for business forms, data workflows, dashboards and internal tools. Smaller, clearly scoped projects start at KSh 40,000 or $400. I am John Mwaura, known as Dev John, an independent full-stack developer in Kenya. When a business workflow needs its own software A spreadsheet can hold records, but it may become difficult to manage when several people need to update them or follow different rules. A custom application can put the forms, records and actions in one place. The useful starting point is the task that staff repeat and the information they need to complete it. Internal tools can cover order workflows, booking processes or administrative tasks. Dashboards can bring relevant records into a readable view. Role-based access can control which parts people use when that is part of the requirements. These are possible project directions, with the actual features defined in the scope. Smaller projects and advanced platforms The Custom Software package starts at KSh 40,000 or $400 for smaller, clearly scoped projects. It lists custom functionality, business forms and data-management workflows, a suitable admin interface where required, basic reporting or dashboards where appropriate, a responsive web interface, deployment and handover. That starting figure is not a price for an entire marketplace or SaaS product. Advanced Platforms and Custom Products uses a custom quote for multi-vendor marketplaces, SaaS, booking and reservation platforms, business management systems, advanced dashboards and complex API integrations. The boundary depends on what the product must do. A limited form and reporting workflow can have a clear edge. A platform with several kinds of users, linked transactions and many external dependencies needs a broader discussion. I would rather define those parts in writing before attaching a package name to the project. How I scope an application Describe one current process using a real example with sensitive information removed. Explain who starts it, which records they enter, what another person reviews and what result is needed. If different people have different access, describe those responsibilities in ordinary language. We can then identify the forms, data, admin screens and connections the project needs. The written scope and quote provide a reference for the build and review. An existing system may need integration work; a new product may need its database designed from the beginning. https://devjohn.site/services/whatsapp-automation/
WhatsApp automation for business
I use the WhatsApp Cloud API to build lead capture, order workflows, notifications and connections to business tools. I am John Mwaura, known as Dev John, a developer in Kenya. Pricing follows the custom software tier or a custom quote, depending on the agreed scope. Start with the work behind the conversation A customer message often contains information that someone then copies into another place. An automation project starts by identifying that information and the action it should trigger. It might create an enquiry record, pass an order into a business workflow or send a notification when a record changes. The useful outcome needs to be specific. “Automate WhatsApp” is too broad to define a build. “Capture the service requested and put it into the existing enquiry tool” describes a workflow we can discuss. The conversation, the destination system and the expected action all belong in the scope. How the WhatsApp Cloud API fits The WhatsApp Cloud API lets business software connect with WhatsApp messages. In practical terms, an application can receive information from a conversation and use it in a defined workflow. It can also connect updates in a business tool to an agreed notification flow. An API is the software connection between those parts. It does not decide your business process for you. Before choosing the automation, we need to understand what customers send, how the business handles it now and which tool should hold the resulting information. Provider account access and message requirements need review for the actual project. Examples of workflows to discuss Lead capture can begin with a person asking about a service. The relevant details could be recorded for follow-up rather than copied manually from a chat. This is a possible use, with the questions, fields and destination agreed before development. For order taking, explain what identifies an item and which customer details the business needs. An automation can connect the conversation to an order workflow, but the required product data and order handling must be defined. A full online store may also need the e-commerce development service . Notifications start from an event, such as a change in an order record. The discussion needs to identify the event, the intended recipient and the information in the update. Syncing with another tool also depends on the API access available in that tool, rather than a promise that every system can be connected. The Karen West packaging portfolio includes WhatsApp quote requests. A quote link and an API-driven workflow have different scopes; these project entries help make that distinction concrete. Price and project preparation Smaller, clearly scoped custom software starts at KSh 40,000 or $400. Larger workflows, complex API integrations and advanced dashboards need a custom quote. The final price depends on the agreed functionality; there is no separate fixed WhatsApp automation package on my pricing list. Before contacting me, write out a sample conversation and the result you want from it. Remove private customer details. List the business tools involved and describe how staff would use the information after it arrives. If a notification is needed, explain what event should trigger it. That description is more helpful than a long list of imagined features. It lets us discuss the data, the integration and the review criteria together. We agree the scope and written quote before the build, with no assumed delivery time or ongoing service fee published here. WhatsApp automation questions Can you connect WhatsApp to existing tools? Yes. Connecting customer workflows with existing business tools is part of my WhatsApp automation service. The specific connection depends on the tool and the API access available. Is a WhatsApp button the same as automation? No. A button opens a conversation. Automation uses the WhatsApp Cloud API and application logic to handle agreed actions such as capturing records or sending updates. What does WhatsApp automation cost? https://devjohn.site/privacy/
Privacy policy
This page explains how devjohn.site handles information sent through the project form and contact links. I use the information you send to read and reply to your enquiry. You can contact me by email to ask for deletion. Information in the project form The form asks for your name, email, phone number, company, service, budget, timeline and project message. The company field is optional. Please include the project details needed for an enquiry and avoid sending passwords or other access credentials. The form is sent through Web3Forms . That service processes the submission so it can be delivered to me. Its privacy policy describes its own handling of submitted information. WhatsApp, email and external links WhatsApp links open WhatsApp, sometimes with a draft message you can edit before sending. Email links open your email application. Those services handle the messages you send through them under their own policies. Links to GitHub, LinkedIn, live projects and ABC Systems take you to other websites. The contact form does not submit when you simply follow one of those links. Browser storage and resources The site stores your light or dark theme choice in your browser using local storage. You can remove it through your browser settings. The site does not include an analytics script or a tracking cookie banner. Page fonts load from Google Fonts. Technology icons on the homepage and About page load from a public CDN. These resource requests go to those providers when your browser loads the resources. Deletion requests Email mwaura.ke.john@gmail.com if you want to ask about or request deletion of information you sent to me. Include enough context to identify the enquiry. Do not send additional sensitive details for this purpose.
